title: Credits & sources
text: Help This is a fan guide. The game belongs to its authors; the data here was read from the ROM and from the community.

title: The hack
text: Pokémon Hyper Emerald: Lost Artifacts (口袋妖怪 究极绿宝石) is the work of its Chinese authors: Destvol, Satochu, Popy, Potato, Hurricane, Feiyixiang and their team. It is built on Pokémon Emerald and was originally released through Baidu. Previous translation team All the credits for the previous translation and for fixing the earlier bugs go to Luciano Fire, Helper, Gustavo Neves and Li Yun . Their community English translation (up to Champion Island) is the foundation this build stands on; the patch only continues their work.

title: The English + QoL patch
text: Binary patches on the "bugfix 2" build of v5.7, with no source access: full translation of the remaining text, bag sort, 999 stack cap, four registered key items, quick ball throw, auto-run, L quick repel, in-party move relearner, and coloured stat names. Tools: mGBA (with Lua scripting for automated tests), Capstone, Keystone, Python. Scripts, tools, docs and translation data are MIT-licensed; the game and the hack are not covered and are not distributed. Repository: github.com/Nn-Exe/Pokemon-Hyper-Emerald-5.7-QoL . The engineering log with every address and hook is in docs/NOTES.md .

title: Where the guide's data comes from
text: Wild encounters, trainer teams, map names, item and species lists : read directly from the patched ROM with the scripts in the repository. These are the same bytes the game uses, so they are exact for v5.7 bugfix 2. Story, quest steps and NPC hints : reconstructed from the game's dialogue (the translated text) and checked against community playthroughs where possible. Legendary and Mega Stone locations : community guides for v5.5–v5.6 (listed below), cross-checked with the dialogue and the ROM's script data. Anything that could not be confirmed for v5.7 is marked as unverified on its page.

title: Reporting mistakes
text: If a level, location or step here is wrong, open an issue on the repository with a screenshot. The guide pages are plain HTML in the repository's docs/ folder, so pull requests are welcome too. Previous FAQ & known issues Back to Overview

title: FAQ & known issues
text: Help Patch problems, save problems, and the hack's own quirks. Check here before assuming your ROM is broken.

title: "this is not the expected original ROM"
text: Your file is not the "bugfix 2" build of v5.7. Check the SHA-1 against f785bed9d9e82e8da13ea4a5ad747e3ea4ec7ba9 (see Install & play ). Vanilla Emerald is 16 MB; the hack is 32 MB. The older community English ROM will also be refused: the patch already contains the full translation, so it has to start from the untouched Chinese ROM.

title: Can I apply this on top of another patch or cheat-modified ROM?
text: No. The patcher compares every byte it changes with what it expects, so any other modification makes it stop. Apply to a clean ROM and add cheats as emulator codes instead.

title: Does it need the translation-only build first?
text: No. The release patch goes from the Chinese ROM straight to the final build in one step.

title: My save is gone after switching to the new ROM
text: Emulators match the .sav by file name. Rename either the ROM or the save so the base names match. The save data itself is compatible in both directions.

title: Can I use save states from the old ROM?
text: No. Save states capture the whole ROM image and memory, so they only work with the exact ROM they were made on. Save in-game, switch ROMs, then load the battery save.

title: Will future patch versions break my save?
text: The QoL features keep their state in bytes the game never used and the save format is untouched, so updates are designed to be save-compatible. Keep a backup of the .sav anyway.

title: The hack's own known issues
text: These come from the hack, not from the patch, and were reported by players of v5.5–v5.7. Workarounds where known: Problem What to do Softlock or freeze with the sound mode set to Stereo Set sound to Mono in the in-game Options menu. Reported for several versions. No experience after the Elite Four in some saves Linked to the trainer-level / obedience system; check that your trainer level is high enough for your Pokémon's level and keep progressing the post-game story. Save often. Crash when catching certain Pokémon with a Master Ball Use another ball on legendaries where possible, or save before throwing. Crash in the post-game Xerneas encounter (older versions) Fixed in the "bugfix" builds of v5.7. Make sure your base ROM is bugfix 2. Shop purchase soft-resets the game Only happens for shops that the hack's custom mart code does not know; the retail shops are fine. This is why the patch does not add a Rare Candy shop. The bag freezes when the cursor lands on one item Press SELECT to skip over that item, then B to leave the bag. Save disappears after the League (PC emulators) Set the emulator's save type to Flash 128K ; the hack needs the full 128 KB save. Evolution by stone does n

title: I still see a few Chinese lines
text: About 50 strings are intentionally left in Chinese: link-battle and Trainer Card messages that end in a page-break control (rewriting those can hang the text engine), a few short name-table entries without context, and text baked into images such as the title logo. If you see Chinese dialogue during normal play, report it with a screenshot on the GitHub issues page .

title: A stat-boost message from an X item is not coloured
text: The hack draws that message inside the bag window with its own routine that ignores colour codes. Stat changes from moves and abilities are coloured.

title: R does nothing in battle
text: Quick throw only works in wild single battles at the action menu, with at least one ball in the Poké Balls pocket and room in the party or PC. It is disabled in trainer, Safari, double, link and Battle Frontier battles.

title: R does not toggle running
text: You need the Running Shoes, and the map must allow running (as in vanilla, you cannot run inside most buildings).

title: L does nothing
text: Either a repel is already active or you carry none. The hack's own "use another?" prompt still appears when a repel wears off.

title: The relearner returns me to the overworld
text: That is expected; the game's relearner exits to the field. Open the party menu again to continue.

title: Is the hack complete?
text: Yes. v5.7 is a finished release with Hoenn, Sinnoh and the post-game. The English patch has been played through the areas its tests cover, not all forty-plus hours, so odd text is still possible in deep post-game screens.

title: Where do I get the ROM?
text: The guide and the repository do not distribute ROMs. Get the hack from its original release thread and patch it yourself. Previous Mega Stones & key items Next Credits & sources

title: QoL features & controls
text: Start here What the English + QoL patch adds on top of the hack, and which button does what. All of it works on existing saves.

title: Controls at a glance
text: Where Button What happens Overworld R Toggle auto-run on/off (sound cue plays) Overworld L Offer to use a Repel (Max → Super → Repel) Overworld SELECT Use the registered key item, or pick one of up to four Bag START Sort the current pocket (type → name → amount) Bag SELECT Move an item (unchanged from the hack) Bag ◀ ▶ Switch pockets (the hack uses the D-pad, not L/R) Wild battle, action menu R tap Throw the first ball in your Poké Balls pocket Wild battle, action menu R hold + ◀ ▶ See the ball and count, pick another ball Party menu Moves option Open the Move Relearner for that Pokémon, no Heart Scale

title: Full English text
text: Roughly 6,000 strings that were still Chinese in the community translation are now English: the post-game and Lost Artifacts story (Volo and Arceus), the Sinnoh region, every Pokédex entry for all 960 species, item, ability and move descriptions, Battle Frontier text and trainer dialogue. About 50 strings stay Chinese on purpose (link-battle and Trainer Card messages whose control codes can hang the text engine, a few name-table entries with no context, and image-baked text such as the title art). Pokédex entries, including Gen 4–8 species.

title: Bag sort
text: Press START in any bag pocket. Each press cycles the sort order: type (the game's internal item order) → name → amount . A message in the description box confirms the mode. The order is written to the bag itself, so it stays sorted after you close the menu. START cycles type, name and amount.

title: Bag stack cap 999
text: Every pocket now holds up to 999 of an item (the hack allowed 99, except Berries). The quantity column shows three digits. The shop's buy picker still stops at 99 per purchase, so buy twice if you want more. Three-digit quantities.

title: Register up to four key items
text: In the Key Items pocket, Register works on up to four items; every registered item shows the SEL marker. In the overworld, SELECT behaves as in vanilla when only one item is registered. With two or more, a popup lists them on ▲ ▶ ▼ ◀ ; press a direction to use that item, or B/SELECT to cancel. The hack's Mach Bike ↔ Acro Bike swap works on every slot. The directional popup with three items registered.

title: Quick ball throw
text: In a wild single battle, at the Fight/Bag/Pokémon/Run menu: Tap R to throw the ball in slot 1 of your Poké Balls pocket without opening the bag. Hold R to see the ball name and count. While holding, ◀ ▶ rotates the pocket so a different ball becomes the default (this reorders the pocket, so it persists in the save). A long hold or a cycle releases without throwing. A ball icon with a red "R" badge at the bottom-left of the screen marks that the feature is available. Disabled in trainer, Safari, double, link and Battle Frontier battles, when you have no balls, and when both party and PC are full. The R badge shows during the action menu.

title: Auto-run toggle
text: Press R in the overworld to toggle. When on, walking becomes running without holding B, and holding B walks instead. The setting is saved with your game. It respects the Running Shoes and any map where running is not allowed (buildings, some caves), exactly like vanilla.

title: L quick repel
text: Press L in the overworld. The game asks "Use the Max Repel?", falling back to Super Repel and then Repel depending on what you carry. It does nothing while a repel is already active or when you have none. When a repel wears off, the hack's own "use another?" prompt appears; that was already part of Hyper Emerald. One press, one confirmation. The hack's native "use another?" prompt.

title: In-party move relearner
text: Open the party menu, pick a Pokémon, and choose Moves . The game's Move Relearner opens for that Pokémon with the hack's expanded move lists, and no Heart Scale is consumed. When you finish you return to the overworld rather than the party menu. Party menu → Moves.

title: Coloured stat names
text: In every "rose" / "fell" battle message the stat name is coloured: Attack red, Defense orange, Speed light green, Sp. Atk pink, Sp. Def blue, Accuracy and Evasiveness yellow. The X-item message the hack shows inside the bag window is drawn by the hack's own routine and stays plain. Swords Dance and Tail Whip.

title: Things that were investigated and left out
text: Bigger Items pocket / PC storage : the hack stores its own flag tables in the old bag area of the save, so growing the pocket would corrupt saves. Rare Candy shop : the hack's shop code only handles its own mart lists and soft-resets on any other purchase. OHKO as an in-game item : delivered as an emulator cheat instead (see Install & play ). PC item sort : written but never verified in the emulator, so it is not in the release patch. Previous Install & play Next Game mechanics

title: Install & play
text: Start here Get the right ROM, apply the English + quality-of-life patch, and set up an emulator. Takes about five minutes. Read this first: which ROM to patch The patch only works on the Chinese hack itself , the "bugfix 2" build of Hyper Emerald: Lost Artifacts v5.7. It does not work on vanilla Pokémon Emerald (USA), on other Hyper Emerald versions (v5.5, v5.6, v5.7 without bugfix, bugfix 1), or on the older community English translation. Start from the untouched Chinese ROM.

title: What you need
text: Base ROM Hyper EMR LA v5.7 bugfix 2.gba (the hack's own release; game code BPEE ) Size 33,554,432 bytes (32 MB, twice the size of vanilla Emerald) SHA-1 f785bed9d9e82e8da13ea4a5ad747e3ea4ec7ba9 Patch release/hyper-emerald-en-qol.hpatch from the GitHub repository Tool Python 3 (no extra packages) to run tools/romdiff.py Result SHA-1 fa19d312ce155e30f31dc1461f21027c54d05405 ; the tool verifies this for you Check your file's hash before patching: # Windows certutil -hashfile "Hyper EMR LA v5.7 bugfix 2.gba" SHA1 # Linux / macOS sha1sum "Hyper EMR LA v5.7 bugfix 2.gba"

title: Apply the patch
text: Download the repository Use "Code → Download ZIP" on GitHub, or clone it. You need tools/romdiff.py and release/hyper-emerald-en-qol.hpatch . Run the patcher python tools/romdiff.py apply "Hyper EMR LA v5.7 bugfix 2.gba" release/hyper-emerald-en-qol.hpatch "Hyper Emerald v5.7 EN+QoL.gba" The tool refuses to run on the wrong original ("this is not the expected original ROM") and checks the output's checksum when it finishes. Play Load the new .gba in mGBA, RetroArch (mGBA core), or any GBA emulator. See the platform notes below.

title: PC (mGBA or RetroArch)
text: mGBA is the reference emulator; everything in the patch was tested on it. Any recent build works. RetroArch : use the mGBA core. Other GBA cores generally work too, but the optional cheat file is written for mGBA. The hack runs at normal GBA speed; fast-forward is safe and does not break scripted events.

title: Android handhelds
text: RetroArch with the mGBA core, or standalone mGBA, both run the hack well on low-end chips. Put the ROM and its .sav in the same folder with the same base name.

title: Nintendo Switch (homebrew mGBA)
text: mGBA 0.10.x for Switch runs the hack. Copy the ROM to your SD card and keep the file name stable so the save is picked up. Set savegamePath in /mGBA/config.ini if you want several ROM builds to share one save folder.

title: Saves and save states
text: Your old save keeps working Battery saves ( .sav ) transfer between the original Chinese hack, the older translation-only builds and this build in either direction. The patch never touches code that reads or writes the save; the new features keep their state in bytes the game never used. Emulators match saves by ROM file name . Either name the new ROM exactly like the old one, or rename the .sav to match the new ROM. Save states ( .ss0 , .state ) do not transfer between ROM builds. Do an in-game save before switching ROMs, then load the battery save. Keep a copy of your .sav before trying cheats or a new build. It is a 128 KB file; backups are cheap.

title: Optional cheats
text: The repository ships one cheat: it pins your active Pokémon's Attack, Sp. Atk and Speed to 9999 in battle (a one-hit-KO helper for grinding). It is a RAM code, so it changes nothing in the ROM or your save. mGBA : copy cheats/OHKO.cheats next to the ROM and rename it to <rom name>.cheats . mGBA loads it automatically; toggle it in Tools → Cheats. RetroArch : put cheats/Hyper Emerald v5.7.cht in the core's cheat folder and enable it from Quick Menu → Cheats. Do not use HP-lock or "infinite HP" codes Codes that pin the foe's HP make it impossible to faint them, because the game's faint check runs a few frames after HP reaches zero. The shipped cheat pins stats instead, which is safe.

title: Rebuilding the patch yourself
text: Every feature is a standalone Python patcher that checks the exact bytes it expects before writing. The repository README lists the order; you need keystone-engine , capstone and pillow . Most players never need this. Previous Overview Next QoL features & controls

title: Pokémon Hyper Emerald: Lost Artifacts v5.7
text: Unofficial fan guide Two regions, sixteen gyms, every Pokémon through Generation 8, and an English + quality-of-life patch to play it all with. This guide covers installing the patch, every added feature, and a walkthrough from Littleroot Town to the end of the post-game. 2 Regions 16 Gyms 898+ Pokémon 3 Leagues

title: What is Hyper Emerald?
text: Hyper Emerald: Lost Artifacts (究极绿宝石) is a Chinese ROM hack of Pokémon Emerald by Destvol, Satochu, Popy, Potato, Hurricane, Feiyixiang and others. On top of the Hoenn story it adds the whole Sinnoh region as post-game, a third "league" of challenges, Mega Evolution, Z-Moves and Dynamax/Gigantamax, all species up to Sword and Shield with their Gen 8 moves and abilities, a trainer-level system, over a hundred side quests, and a hard mode. The 32 MB ROM is twice the size of the original game. The earlier English translation and its bug fixes are the work of Luciano Fire, Helper, Gustavo Neves and Li Yun ; this build continues from there. The English + QoL patch finishes the English translation (about 6,000 strings that the community translation had left in Chinese) and adds modern conveniences: bag sorting, 999-item stacks, four registered key items, one-button ball throws, auto-run, a one-button repel, an in-party move relearner and coloured stat names. Existing saves keep working.

title: How this guide was made
text: The reference pages are generated from the patched ROM: wild encounter tables, trainer parties, map names and item lists are read from the game's own data tables, so they match what you meet in play. The walkthrough and quest pages are written from the game's dialogue and from community playthroughs; where a step could not be verified in v5.7 it is marked. Corrections are welcome on the repository . A note on spoilers The walkthrough pages describe the story as it happens. The reference pages (trainers, locations, legendaries, items) list post-game content without warning. If you want to go in blind, stick to the Hoenn walkthrough until you are Champion. Also see Credits & sources Next Install & play

ROM Enamorus — Cogita, once you own the other three. ROM Meloetta — Joins after the Hearthome Contest Spectacular; a Relic Song tutor exists. ROM Glastrier / Spectrier / Calyrex 50 Crown Shrine (the radish field in the snow); the priest gives the bond rope. ROM Zacian 50 Iron Island after the gatekeeper and the two heroes. ROM Zamazenta — Paired with Zacian's story; not found as a separate script. community Regieleki / Regidrago 50 Ruins of Decision: Regieleki with an Electric type in the party (Route 209 ruins); Regidrago with a Flygon holding the Draco Plate in slot one (Lake Acuity ruins). RO

title: Every scripted encounter in the ROM
text: The complete list of fixed wild battles found by scanning the map scripts (not only legendaries). Useful for the strong wild Pokémon that guard some areas. Pokémon Lv Held item Map Region Previous Pokémon locations Next Mega Stones & key items

title: Game mechanics
text: Start here The hack changes a lot under the hood. These are the rules you need to know before you pick a starter, and the systems you will keep running into. Decide your difficulty before you leave the bedroom The difficulty is chosen at the wall clock in your bedroom at the start of the game and cannot be changed afterwards. See the modes below.

title: Difficulty modes
text: Four modes exist. The fourth is hidden: interact with the notebook next to the PC in your bedroom and pick the red "Not Ready" option ten times, then use the clock. Mode Level cap Items in battle Other rules Easy (养生) None Allowed Plays like an official game. Legendaries allowed everywhere. Standard (标准) Tied to badges (about Lv 18 before Gym 1, Lv 23 after) Allowed in the field; formal battles ban them Gyms and leagues: no duplicate species or held items, no box legendaries or mythicals. Challenge (挑战) As Standard Banned in trainer battles The AI sometimes predicts your move. Lunatic (疯子, hidden) As Standard Banned Every trainer has perfect IVs and full EVs; the AI predicts most moves. Community guides for v5.5 (17173, the Portuguese v5.5 guide); the exact cap numbers may differ slightly in v5.7.

title: Level caps and obedience
text: In every mode except Easy, Pokémon stop gaining experience at the current cap . The cap rises with each badge and league win. Pokémon above the cap disobey , and you cannot catch Pokémon that are too strong for your current badge count. An NPC in Sinnoh puts it plainly: "Since I've only got one Gym Badge, it sometimes ignores my orders." Gym and league battles follow tournament rules. Status moves are unreliable there: "In battles against Gym Leaders and the Hoenn League's Elite Four, moves that inflict status conditions and the like have no effect." Shops unlock stock by badge count (Revives, for example). Consumable items used in trainer battles are given back afterwards.

title: Starters and early gifts
text: On the starter screen press ▶ to page through all 24 starters from Kanto to Galar. Hisuian lines appear as Cyndaquil, Oshawott and Rowlet; picking one of those gets you a second starter from Professor Birch after you beat your rival. The Hoenn trio can be caught later in a pen at the lab once you have the Running Shoes, with three perfect IVs. Your PC starts with a Shiny Charm, an EV/IV display item and Power items. Petalburg Woods: Professor Oak offers a Let's Go Pikachu or Eevee (they do not evolve; a tutor in Fortree teaches their partner moves). Route 104: an NPC gives a Wimpod . Rustboro, house top-right of the gym: trade for a Zorua ; the same NPC swaps Zorua between its Unovan and Hisuian forms.

title: Battle systems added by the hack
Mega Evolution
text: Needs the Mega Bracelet : after beating Norman, talk to your mother in Littleroot. Her line: "This is a gift that the president of Devon asked your father to pass along… Your father thought it was still too early for you to receive such a precious band, so he left it with me!" Mega Stones are hidden items and rewards; see Mega Stones & key items .

title: Z-Moves
text: Needs the Z-Ring , won from the trainer behind the Fortree City Pokémon Center. Z-Crystals come from the 18 Totem Pokémon hidden around Hoenn; collecting all 18 is also a story gate in the post-game.

title: Dynamax and Gigantamax
text: Opens in the post-game on World Championship Island, where Leon (or Sonia, if you missed him) hands you the Dynamax Band . Dynamax is only possible at Power Spots (the Championship battles, Leon's rematches, some story fights). Gigantamax forms come from Max Mushrooms and a Max Soup NPC on the island, who treats the first Pokémon in your party.

title: Other combat changes
text: Moves, abilities and items through Generation 8; turn order is recalculated mid-turn as in Sword and Shield. Trainer AI is stronger across the board; the higher modes let it read your move. Formal battles (gyms, leagues, the World Championships) use tournament rules: exactly six Pokémon brought, pick three or four, doubles for the Sinnoh League and Championships.

title: Training and quality of life
text: What How Exp. Share Built in: full experience to battlers, half to the bench. "It works just by sitting in your Bag." EVs / IVs The whole team gets EVs. An EV checker and an IV judge stand at the Solaceon Day Care; the starting PC has a display item. TMs and HMs Reusable. HM moves work from the bag without teaching them (Flash excepted). Every TM can be bought on World Championship Island after the Sinnoh League. Nature change Trainer's School in Rustboro: answer 8 of 10 quiz questions, then pick a nature (mints are sold at the Lilycove Department Store). Ability change Ability Pill (regular abilities) and Ability Patch (hidden ability) drop as held items from Zigzagoon on Route 101. Professor Sycamore also sells them for Zygarde Cells. Trade evolutions Talk to the boy in the house east of Fallarbor and answer "No" (counts as a trade); an NPC in the Fortree Pokémon Center does the same. Hold the required item first. Move relearner The patch adds a Moves option in the party menu (no Heart Scale). The hack's own tutors want Heart Scales; farm them from Luvdisc with the Old Rod. Egg moves Inherited as in Sword and Shield. Bikes Mach and Acro Bikes from the house right of the Mauville

title: Getting around
text: Hoenn : as vanilla, plus a ride device and a "news searcher" gadget that reports where roaming Pokémon are. Sinnoh : every town has Ride Pokémon that fly you between towns you have visited. The summoning device is in the Team Galactic warehouse in Veilstone. Bibarel climbs rock walls with the ride gear; Route 206 requires a rented bike from the Eterna bike shop (pass the assistant's exam first). Hisui : Rei is the fast-travel NPC between the safe zones, and his Rotom PC gives you box access.

title: Things closed or cosmetic
text: The Global Terminal, Trade Hall, Veilstone Game Corner and Seven Stars Restaurant in Sinnoh are decorative. The World Championship tournament itself is a placeholder in v5.7 ("The World Championships will officially open in the future"); the island hosts cameo battles and Dynamax Power Spots. Sprites occasionally glitch after warps. An NPC explains it: "If this happens, just switch screens and it will go back to normal." Previous QoL features & controls Next Walkthrough: Hoenn

title: Pokémon locations
text: Reference Every wild encounter table in the ROM: grass, surfing, Rock Smash and fishing, with levels and slot odds. Type a Pokémon or a place. How to read the odds Percentages are the fixed slot odds of the Emerald engine (grass: 20, 20, 10, 10, 10, 10, 5, 5, 4, 4, 1, 1). Fishing rows are grouped by rod. "Rate" is the per-step encounter rate for that terrain. Static encounters, gifts, trades and legendaries are on the Legendary Pokémon page and in the walkthrough. By location By Pokémon loading encounter data…

title: Gym Leaders & bosses
text: Reference Teams read straight from the ROM's trainer table: species, level, held item and moves where the trainer has custom ones. Use it to plan a gym before you walk in. About levels The hack scales some boss fights with its difficulty setting and trainer-level system; the numbers here are what the ROM's trainer table stores for the normal encounter. Where a trainer has several entries (rematches, hard mode), every version is listed. loading trainer data…

title: Every trainer in the ROM
text: The complete trainer table, for anyone checking a specific route battle. Collapsed by default. Show all trainers

title: Hoenn: Littleroot to Champion
text: Walkthrough · Part 1 The main story follows Emerald's route, so this page focuses on what the hack adds or changes at each stop, and shows every gym leader's actual team from the ROM. How to use this page Steps that are identical to vanilla Emerald are summarised in a line. Anything new gets its own paragraph. Level caps below assume Standard mode; on Easy there are none. Wild encounter tables for every route are on the Pokémon locations page.

title: Littleroot Town
text: Start Set the clock = pick your difficulty. It cannot be changed later. For the hidden Lunatic mode, use the notebook by the PC ten times first. See Game mechanics . Your PC already holds a Shiny Charm, an EV/IV display item and Power items. Route 101: press ▶ on the starter screen to scroll through all 24 starters. The Route 101 Zigzagoon carry the Ability Pill and Ability Patch as held items; come back with Thief later. Route 103 rival battle, then the Pokédex and Poké Balls as usual. Ralts on Route 102 have Synchronize.

title: Petalburg, Petalburg Woods, Rustboro
text: Badge 1 · cap Lv 18 Petalburg Gym is locked until you have four badges, as in vanilla. Wally's catching tutorial happens here. Petalburg Woods: Professor Oak appears and offers a Let's Go Pikachu or Eevee. On Route 104 an NPC gives a Wimpod. Scizorite is hidden in the woods. Rustboro: the Trainer's School NPC changes natures once you pass their quiz. The house top-right of the gym trades a Zorua. Devon Corp 2F has Pidgeotite; Magearna waits behind the receptionist's door much later in the game.

title: Gym 1: Roxanne (Rock)
text: Six Pokémon at level 18 with hazards (Stealth Rock, Sticky Web, Toxic Spikes) and Eviolite fossils. Bring Grass or Water and a way to remove hazards; Rock Tomb is your reward. Devon parcel errand as vanilla: Rusturf Tunnel, then Mr. Stone gives the PokéNav and the letter for Steven.

title: Dewford, Granite Cave, Slateport
text: Badge 2 · cap Lv 23 Granite Cave: deliver the letter to Steven; a miner gives Flash. The Earth Plate is in a side cave at the deepest part of 1F (you can only use it much later).

title: Gym 2: Brawly (Fighting)
text: Hisuian Sneasler and Lucario make this a mixed Fighting/Poison and Steel wall. Flying and Psychic moves, and a Fairy type if you have one, carry the fight. Slateport: the Contest Hall and Museum play out as vanilla; the shipyard's second floor had a freeze in older versions, fixed in v5.7 bugfix builds. Route 110 rival battle. Manectite is hidden along the Cycling Road side.

title: Mauville
text: Badge 3 · cap Lv 28 The house right of the Pokémon Center gives both bikes; swap between Mach and Acro any time. Wally battles you at the gym entrance with a Kirlia.

title: Gym 3: Wattson (Electric)
text: Six level-28 Electric types including Rotom and Magnezone. Ground types are immune to most of it; Pincurchin and Rotom will still hurt. Wattson is a known wall on the harder modes.

title: Side quest: the Team Rocket hideout under the Game Corner
text: The Skitty errand in Mauville leads to a hidden Team Rocket base beneath the Game Corner . Two door passwords are needed, typed in capitals: ARCHER on the first floor, then ROCKET for the second-floor check, answered No / Yes / No. Inside you fight a Rocket researcher with a level-40 "DNA" Eevee that transforms, and you can catch the special DNA Eevee afterwards (it is treated as a 3-badge Pokémon for obedience). The base also holds the Iron Plate and Dread Plate . The Eevee misbehaves and loses HP each turn until you receive an item that triggers automatically at the exit of Victory Road later in the story. Community reports for v5.5–5.7 (pokeharbor comments, 9game); the plate placement is confirmed by the Sinnoh plate hints in the game text.

title: Route 111 to Fallarbor, Meteor Falls, Mt. Chimney
text: Badge 4 · cap Lv 37 Fallarbor: the house east of town holds the "trade" NPC (answer No to evolve trade-evolution Pokémon). Galladite is in Professor Cozmo's house. Meteor Falls: Team Magma and Aqua fight over the meteorite as vanilla. Salamencite is on 1F and Aerodactylite deeper in. A locked Draconid cave here matters in the post-game (Draco Plate, Steven, Cosmog). Mt. Chimney: cable car up, then Maxie with Tabitha and Courtney. Zinnia already fights here as a Team Magma member. Jagged Pass has Tyranitarite.

title: Gym 4: Flannery (Fire)
text: Hisuian Typhlosion and Arcanine, Charizard and Cinderace at level 37. Water and Rock coverage, and a Rotom answer, are enough. Go-Goggles for the desert follow.

title: Petalburg again
text: Badge 5 · cap Lv 45

title: Gym 5: Norman (Normal)
text: Six level-45 Pokémon with Snorlax, Ursaluna and a Hisuian Zoroark. Fighting types are the answer to everything except the Zoroark; watch for its Illusion. Mega Bracelet After the badge, go home to Littleroot and talk to your mother. She gives the Mega Bracelet , a gift from Devon your father held back. Wally's father gives Surf as usual.

title: Route 118, Weather Institute, Fortree
text: Badge 6 · cap Lv 51 Weather Institute: Team Aqua, Shelly, and Castform as in vanilla. The rival fights you on Route 119 afterwards with a full team of six. Fortree: the trainer behind the Pokémon Center hands over the Z-Ring when beaten. The Pokémon Center also has a trade-evolution NPC and a tutor for the Let's Go partner moves. Garchompite is in town.

title: Gym 6: Winona (Flying)
text: Celesteela and Dragonite raise the ceiling to level 51. Ice and Rock moves, and Electric for the rest.

title: Routes 120–121, Mt. Pyre, Lilycove, Mossdeep
text: Badge 7 · cap Lv 57 Route 120: Scorched Slab holds Charizardite X. Kecleon ambushes on 119/120 as vanilla. Mt. Pyre: Gengarite lies between two of the four stones in the foggy area. The wild Pokémon on the Route 122 side carry evolution stones to steal. Lilycove: rival battle with six Pokémon, then the Team Aqua hideout (Matt). The Department Store sells mints. Mossdeep: the gym is blocked by an NPC until you finish a short Shoal Cave quest (battle Hugh and Team Plasma). Slowbronite is on Shoal Cave 1F; Pinsirite on the left side of Mossdeep.

title: Gym 7: Tate & Liza (Psychic, Double Battle)
text: Two Indeedee run Psychic Terrain support for Metagross, Gallade and Gardevoir. Dark and Ghost attackers, or a Steel wall, do well; spread moves earn their keep.

title: Seafloor Cavern, Sootopolis, Sky Pillar
text: Badge 8 · cap Lv 62 Space Center, Seafloor Cavern and Archie's Kyogre play out as vanilla. Archie's team is below. Sootopolis: Groudon and Kyogre clash; Steven sends you to the Cave of Origin, then Wallace to the Sky Pillar on Route 131. The Sky Pillar needs the Mach Bike (swap in Mauville). Rayquaza calms the two and you receive Waterfall.

title: Gym 8: Juan (Water)
text: Level 62 with Kingdra, Swampert and Hisuian Basculegion. Grass moves for Swampert and Politoed, Electric for the rest; Kingdra only fears Dragon and Fairy.

title: Victory Road and Ever Grande
text: Elite Four · Level 70 · Double Battles Victory Road needs every HM. Wally fights you inside with five Pokémon in the 75–80 range. At the exit an automatic event fixes the DNA Eevee's condition if you caught it. The Hoenn League in this hack is fought in double battles at level 70 . Bring exactly six Pokémon. Status moves do not work on the Elite Four.

title: Champion Wallace (Water)
text: Before you enter the Hall of Fame An attendant stops you: "we have decided to raise the potential of the first Pokémon in your party to its absolute limit". Put the Pokémon you want with perfect IVs in slot one before the Champion fight.

title: After the credits
text: You wake up at home. Your father gives a ticket for the Battle Frontier, Professor Birch upgrades the Pokédex, and Wally calls to say a Team Magma remnant has attacked him in Petalburg. That call starts the post-game; continue with Post-game: Sinnoh & beyond . Previous Game mechanics Next Post-game: Sinnoh & beyond

title: Lost Artifacts questline
text: Walkthrough · Part 3 The story that names the hack: seventeen Plates scattered across two regions, a choice between time and space, Arceus, and a trip to ancient Hisui to face Volo. This is the last and hardest content in the game. What you need before you start Sinnoh League and the Ultra League cleared. A strong level-100 team. Volo's final fight is six level-100 legendaries in a double battle, with Dynamax. Note-taking: the game itself says "It might take a while, so take your own notes." The Plate list below saves you that.

title: 1. Cynthia and the hidden ruins
text: Near Celestic Town, Cynthia investigates new ruins that appeared when the Ultra Wormholes started: "Perhaps if you gather all the tablets and set them into the empty slots in the underground ruins, something will be revealed." She has heard from Waji , the green-haired keeper of the ruins, that a tablet "records some kind of instruction". One tablet on the way tells you to "leap down from the northwest corner… remember to back up a bit and take a running jump."

title: 2. Waji at the Spear Pillar: the 17 Plates
text: Waji describes each Plate's hiding place in riddles. His words are quoted, with the resolved location beside them. Plate Waji's hint Where Fist Plate "in an underwater ruin covered with ancient writing" Sealed Chamber, Hoenn Sky Plate "inside a cabin full of Wingull" Mr. Briney's cottage, Route 104 Toxic Plate "in a marshland of the Sinnoh region, on top of a little hillock" Great Marsh, Pastoria Earth Plate "on a small island… in a cave at the deepest part of floor 1 of a rock cavern" Granite Cave 1F, Dewford Stone Plate "in a mine in Sinnoh, surrounded by digging machines and ore" Oreburgh Mine Insect Plate "ruins in the Sinnoh region with a tangled, complex layout… inside one of the large caves" Solaceon Ruins Spooky Plate "in a tower in the Sinnoh region, quite close to the ruins of the Insect Plate" Lost Tower Iron Plate and Dread Plate "in a hidden base in the Hoenn region, surrounded by computers and cultivation tanks" The Team Rocket base under the Mauville Game Corner (the Type: Null lab) Flame Plate "at the summit of an active volcano… lava flowing all around" Mt. Chimney Splash Plate "in the ocean of the Hoenn region, surrounded by white reefs, the plate lies underwater"

title: 3. The altar: Dialga or Palkia
text: "As the plate resonated, [you] sensed turbulence in space-time!… Activate the plate's power and enter the rift?" Inside, "[you] must choose between the god of time and the god of space." Whichever you choose is lent to you for the next fight; the other can be reached later at the Celestic ruins community . Both are level-80 encounters in the ROM.

title: 4. The god-king
text: Cyrus has "mastered time and space… and reached the realm of the divine". You must fight him with the borrowed Dialga or Palkia : "You wish to challenge me, the god-king, without even a shred of divine power to match me?" His team is six level-100 Pokémon including both Dialga and Palkia. On defeat he banishes you: "Cast him into the world I once ruled!… Wander that world of void for all eternity!" In the void world an old acquaintance from Petalburg Woods blocks the way home; beat them, and the Lake Guardians and Giratina return you: "Thank you for helping us free Palkia and Dialga… I will send you back to your world." Giratina has wrecked the spatial supports around the Spear Pillar, so leave before it collapses. Waji afterwards: the same energy is now coming from Celestic Town. Go there, and when you return "that altar suddenly changed, and a new passage appeared."

title: 5. Arceus on Mt. Coronet
text: Hard requirement Waji only sends you up once "Dialga, Palkia and Giratina… are now all gathered in one Trainer" and "all 17 scattered shards have also been recovered." You need all three in your possession plus every Plate. At the summit the Plates resonate and Arceus speaks: "I am the one you humans call the God of Creation, Arceus!… let Me first test your current strength!" The trial of Genesis is a battle against Arceus (level 80 in the ROM); losing gets "Unworthy! Our trial is absolute!" Winning: "We acknowledge you! Until the moment the world reaches its end, we shall lend you our strength!" Arceus points you onward: "Go to Jiayuan City and seek out a certain someone." That someone is Cogita .

title: 6. Cogita and the Dawn of Hisui
text: Cogita, a "poet", tells the legend of Hisui and gives you a Hisuian Pokémon. Then: "Allow me to carry you back to that era, to gather the last plate lost amid space and time… Only those recognized by Arceus may pass freely through the rifts." She sends you to the Diamond and Pearl Clans. Prelude Beach. Rei and Akari meet you. Rei is your fast-travel NPC in Hisui ("Come find me when you need to go somewhere else") and his Rotom PC gives you box access. Deertrack Heights base camp. Rei explains: Volo tore open the rifts, was beaten at the Temple of Sinnoh and vanished; now the rifts spawn giant red-glowing Pokémon, which the game treats as Dynamax. Only the safe zones are reachable: Prelude Beach, Deertrack Heights, Firespit Island, the Snowfall hot spring, Coronet Highlands, the settlements and the Primeval Cave. Kleavor's rampage blocks Deertrack Path. Snowfall Hot Spring. Both clan leaders are here. Irida senses Palkia in your party and, after a battle, gives the Lustrous Globe . The wounded Adaman senses Dialga and, after a battle, gives the Adamant Crystal . Bring both legendaries. Both leaders point to the Coronet Highlands. Primeval Cave: Volo. He introduces himself as a Ginkg

title: 7. After the Dawn
text: Akari confirms the distortions are under control; Adaman and Irida invite you to the hot springs. Back home, Cogita hints at a further mystery ("'They' may not be enemies…") and opens the Dream Sky Gauntlet at her retreat in Sootopolis: Cogita, Rei, Akari, Adaman, Irida and Volo in a row, healed between battles. She also grants Enamorus once you own the other three genies. Volo also appears in Hoenn's Sealed Chamber as a Ginkgo merchant selling rare goods, once you have read the Braille there. A blue-haired passer-by offers, for 500,000, to send you "back to the recent past", a New Game Plus style loop. Previous Post-game: Sinnoh & beyond Next Gym Leaders & bosses

title: Post-game: Sinnoh & beyond
text: Walkthrough · Part 2 The post-game is longer than the main story. It runs in three chapters: the Hoenn post-game (Delta Episode, Ultra Wormholes, Team Rainbow Rocket), World Championship Island, and the Sinnoh region. The Arceus story that follows has its own page . Spoilers and sources This page describes the whole story. The order of events and the quotes come from the game's own text; where a step is known only from community playthroughs of v5.5–5.6 it is marked community . Boss teams are read from the ROM.

title: The wake-up
text: Your father gives Ticket 1 for the Battle Frontier; Birch upgrades the Pokédex; trading is unlocked. Wally calls: he is being attacked by a Team Magma remnant in Petalburg. Go there and drive off Magma Admin Courtney. Team Magma's "strongest man" Yanshan waits at the old Magma Hideout and teaches V-create when beaten; the Aqua "empress" waits at the Aqua Hideout. Both are optional.

title: Delta Episode: Zinnia and the meteorite
text: Zinnia's challenge. Zinnia, Lorekeeper of the Draconid people, confronts you as "the hero who awakened Rayquaza" and battles you. Afterwards: "head to the rocket launch center." Mossdeep Space Center. Devon's Infinity Energy powers a probe rocket to survey the incoming meteorite. President Stone explains Plan S (deflect it with the energy) and Plan D, the "Destroyer Meteor". Collect meteorite shards in Granite Cave ; Zinnia intervenes and steals your Mega Bracelet. The twist. At the Space Center Zinnia reveals she and Courtney are the "new Team Magma", grabs the shards and Steven's bracelet, and flees. Steven and Wallace arrest the remnants; you must head for the Sky Pillar. Meteor Falls, the Draconid cave. Fight Zinnia again and get the bracelet back ("The Mega Bracelet has been returned."). Steven battles you here and gives Metagrossite . A Cosmog waits in this cave; it is needed for the Ultra Wormholes and evolves at level 65 into Solgaleo by day or Lunala by night. Sky Pillar. Mach Bike required. Rayquaza pushes the meteoroid away. The Draconid elder at the shrine can re-teach Dragon Ascent. Back in Mossdeep the researchers give you the Meteorite as a memento (you can trade it

title: Steven's island and the Ultra League
text: Reached through the cave beside Ever Grande City once you are Champion. The mansion is the hub for everything that follows. The Ultra League room: Champions from every region are meeting there ("The Champions are inside the residence discussing countermeasures"). You have to beat them one after another to pass ("You must defeat the past Champions to pass!"): Blue, Lance, Alder, Iris, Diantha, Elio and Selene, Gladion, the Kalos champion X, N, Hilda, Black, Lucas, Serena and more. All are level 100; teams are on the trainers page . Anabel (International Police) runs the Ultra Wormhole survey from the conference room. An NPC on the right side of the island gives Beast Balls ; the villa NPC gives the Old Sea Map for Mew on Faraway Island (sail from Lilycove); Selene on the right of the island re-awakens any Totem you beat without collecting its Z-Crystal; a "MoeMoe" attendant gives your lead Pokémon perfect IVs. Grinding spot community : the NPC at the mansion entrance uses level 75–80 Wobbuffet, Blissey, Chansey and Lickitung. Bring Fighting types.

title: Groudon and Kyogre
text: Anabel's first missions: Route 115's Terra Cave , where Maxie fights with a level-100 team and Primal Groudon, giving you the Red Orb and a level-70 Groudon encounter; then the Weather Institute reports an anomaly at Route 125's Marine Cave , where Archie does the same with Kyogre (level 70). Both encounters are scripted battles found in the ROM.

title: Ultra Wormholes
text: Steven at Meteor Falls: "Find Red, the Kanto Champion who defeated an Ultra Beast all on his own, and bring him back to us." The survey NPC tells you where to begin: "let's try starting from the top floor inside Mt. Pyre." Before each wormhole the game saves and warns you to bring medicine and HM users; inside, "certain status-inflicting moves" are useless, and you cannot leave until you finish the other side. You need Cosmog or its evolutions in the party for the spatial gates, or the Ultra Suit (given by the Devon president once Rainbow Rocket is founded; it lets you enter without Solgaleo/Lunala). Mt. Pyre wormhole: an Ultra Recon researcher gives Poipole (evolves by learning Dragon Pulse); Cresselia (level 50) is on Mt. Pyre. Spear Pillar / Distortion World : Cyrus fights you with rental Pokémon; you cannot use your own. Giratina (level 80, holding a Griseous Orb) waits at the end of the Distortion World. New Mauville : Genesect , level 50. Giant Chasm : two Ghetsis fights (doubles, then singles). Rewards: the DNA Splicers and a second Cosmog. Kyurem is here at level 50. Route 116 (Nebel Cave / Timeless Woods) : Volcanion (level 50) and an Eternal Flower Floette . Cerulean Cave

title: Necrozma and the 18 Z-Crystals
text: Anabel: "The light crystals Necrozma scattered across the Hoenn region… have spawned aberrant Totem-like Pokémon… we must gather these light crystals one by one." Eighteen Totem Pokémon (level 80, each holding its type's Z-Crystal) sit in hidden base-style spots around Hoenn; the items page lists them. With all 18: "The 18 Z-Crystals let out a mighty surge…! A suspicious opening seems to have appeared…!" The opening leads to the Pacifidlog Ultra Cave , Faba, Lusamine and the Ultra Null Zone, where Necrozma is "trapped in a prison of lightning". Faba (level 65 doubles) is the boss; Necrozma is a level-50 encounter afterwards, and Faba hands over his research, the N-Solarizer and N-Lunarizer.

title: Team Rainbow Rocket
text: Faba escapes to found Team Rainbow Rocket with villains from parallel worlds. Their base is in Ultra Space (the map is called Rainbow Castle). Bosses in order of the text: Giovanni, Lysandre, Cyrus, an alternate Maxie who "turned my entire world into land", an alternate Archie whose world "ended up swallowed entirely by the sea", Ghetsis with Kyurem and the DNA Splicers, and Faba. Admins Jupiter, Zinzolin, Xerosic, Shelly and Tabitha fight in level-88 doubles. community : on the harder modes Giovanni must be beaten within ten turns, and losing revives you at the base. The arc closes on the Summit of Finality : the assembled Champions rally you ("Believe in the bond between you and your Pokémon, the world will not disappear that easily!") and you fight a giant beast with their aces cheering. Afterwards the original developer's note plays: "You've made it through the Ultra League and Team Rainbow Rocket! Unfortunately, that's all the story progress there is for now." Everything below was added in later versions.

title: Chapter 2: World Championship Island
text: Getting there. Scott gives the ticket after 35 straight wins in the Battle Tower (open level), or after the Rainbow Rocket arc. Sail Slateport → Lilycove → the island. Later the Snowpoint icebreaker in Sinnoh also goes straight to the island. Dynamax Band. Leon was invited by Steven but stayed to fight the Darkest Day; he explains Eternatus "escaped through a spatial distortion" into an Ultra Space in Hoenn and gives the band. If you miss him, Sonia in his room (the small house below the Pokémon Center) gives one. Eternatus. Leon is later found wounded in Ultra Space; you subdue Eternatus alone (level 50 scripted encounter). Leon then offers Dynamax rematches at a Wishing Star power spot; the Max Soup NPC gives your lead Pokémon the Gigantamax factor. Rules. The tournament desk explains the format: standard doubles, bring six choose four, no duplicate species or items, no mythicals. In v5.7 the tournament itself is not open; the island hosts the Galar gym leaders (Bea, Allister, Avery, Klara at level 100 doubles), Koga, Paul and others. Koga's mark. Beat Koga and he marks you. That unlocks the ninja village hidden west of Rustboro: "Please come with only a single Greninja in tow."

title: Arrival
text: Sail from Lilycove to Canalave City . Lucas meets you: "Every town in Sinnoh has Ride Pokémon that can fly you around. But since you're new here, you should visit the towns first." Fly points unlock as you visit. The Ride Pokémon summoner is in the Team Galactic warehouse in Veilstone, which also holds an HM. As Hoenn Champion you may Surf anywhere at once.

title: The eight gyms
text: "Against a Champion's challenge, the Gym Leaders will use power at the mythical tier, and the type restriction drops to a minimum of three Pokémon." Every gym is a level-50 rules battle (bring six, pick three) and can be taken in any order; community guides suggest Canalave first. Each leader gives a Generation 8 TM instead of a badge you need, though the badges still count for the League. title: Sinnoh League
text: Requirements: eight Sinnoh badges, exactly six Pokémon , no eggs. Victory Road: Lucas and Barry meet you at the end; Barry battles, Lucas gives an item. Scripted level-80 pseudo-legendaries (Hydreigon, Salamence, Metagross, Dragonite) live inside. Format: "standard Double Battle rules… The Elite Four await behind the four doors on either side. You may challenge them in any order you like." A staff member heals you between fights and a monitor shows each opponent's team. Aaron (Bug), Bertha (Ground), Flint (Fire) and Lucian (Psychic) are followed by Cynthia in serious mode . The ROM stores only placeholders for these fights; the teams are built at battle time. After the League: Heatran in a new Mt. Coronet opening reached from Snowpoint via Route 216 (level 30 in the ROM); every TM goes on sale at the Championship island.
